Export the estimated distribution of effects for the ebnm package

Source: R/as-normalmix.R
as_normalmix.Rd

as_normalmix() returns the posterior mean of \(g\) as a normalmix object, the class that the ashr and ebnm packages use for a prior distribution that is a mixture of normal distributions. The means of the mixture components are the grid points. The ebnm package can use this object to compute the posterior distributions of the effects with \(g\) fixed at that estimate, so the fit can be compared with empirical Bayes fits of the same data.

Usage

as_normalmix(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

An object of class normalmix, as created by ashr::normalmix(). It is a list with the following components, each with one value per grid point.

pi

The mixture proportions.

mean

The component means, which are the grid points.

sd

The component standard deviations.

Details

The mixture has one component per grid point. The mixture proportions are the posterior means of the probabilities of \(g\). The component standard deviations are zero for a fit with point masses. For a fit with component = "normal", they all equal the standard deviation of its normal components.

Pass the object to ebnm::ebnm_npmle() as g_init with fix_g = TRUE to obtain the plug-in posterior distributions of the effects, in which \(g\) is treated as known. They differ from the posterior distributions of the fit, which average over the posterior draws of \(g\). For most sites the posterior means are close and the standard deviation from the fit is slightly larger, but neither is true for every site. See the Details of site_summary() for the relation between the two standard deviations.

as_normalmix() constructs the object itself, so neither ashr nor ebnm needs to be installed.

See also

g_summary(), site_summary(), vignette("empirical-bayes")

Examples

g <- as_normalmix(krw_fit)
class(g)
#> [1] "normalmix"
# The means of the components are the grid points.
range(g$mean)
#> [1] -0.08289621  0.15852607

# The plug-in posterior distributions, with g fixed at this estimate.
plug_in <- ebnm::ebnm_npmle(krw_discrimination$yi, krw_discrimination$sei,
                            g_init = g, fix_g = TRUE)
sites <- site_summary(krw_fit)
# The posterior means are close for most firms: their absolute
# differences, in units of the posterior standard deviation.
summary(abs(coef(plug_in) - sites$mean) / sites$sd)
#>      Min.   1st Qu.    Median      Mean   3rd Qu.      Max. 
#> 6.254e-05 3.315e-03 6.467e-03 1.458e-02 1.637e-02 2.513e-01 
# The standard deviations from the fit are larger for most firms, but
# not for all.
summary(sites$sd / fitted(plug_in)$sd)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>  0.9818  1.0034  1.0048  1.0039  1.0053  1.0724
